title: Bind stable publication identities to explicit classifier outputs
description:
PLANNING ONLY. Ryan requested filing and design before implementation. This issue is not authorization to build runtime features, deploy, change cloud permissions, publish packages, push, or migrate production data. Keep open pending design review and separate implementation authorization.

As a Papyrus deployment operator, I want an explicit reviewed publication-to-output binding, so that common items can have independent editorial decisions.

Feature: Publication output binding
  Scenario: Same input, different publications
    Given one common item revision and two publications bound to different classifier outputs
    When an operator inspects each publication's decision
    Then each decision identifies its item revision, publication, classifier output and prediction version
    And acceptance by the first publication does not create a label for the second
  Scenario: Ambiguous or changed binding
    Given a missing, ambiguous or changed publication/output binding
    When a publication requests a decision or submits feedback
    Then it receives an explicit binding conflict or required configuration state
    And no output is silently selected or relabeled

Design review / future Definition of Done: review these observable acceptance cases with the shared contract; executable specs and implementation are future work after authorization.
Open: identity namespaces/ownership and lifecycle, mapping cardinality, binding revisions, deduplication versus source identity, and how binding changes affect historical views. Do not assume URL alone is stable identity.

Preserve optional curated-example priming (decision-flywheel-da886c09-7acb-45d3-acf8-c81585f26d8a), its preview/revision/explicit-label acceptance contract, and separate existing scholarly research-paper and web-summary transformations. Priming must never become an onboarding gate. Common input items are distinct from publication-specific decisions; one publication accepting an item must never implicitly label another output.
